subject: Albanese refuses to give direct answer on if copyright laws will be diluted for AI giants
posts:
Prime Minister Anthony Albanese dodges direct questions on whether copyright laws will be diluted for US AI giants ahead of high-stakes talks.
Evidence: Evasive answers, tech lobbying, artist protection rhetoric
#Aletheia #TechPolicy

The government claims unwavering commitment to protecting Australian creators and preventing AI companies from exploiting IP without consent.
Stated Judgement: (+0.9, +0.8) — Greater Good

Behind the protective rhetoric, political leaders equivocate on legislative protections to court massive tech infrastructure investments and appease foreign allies.
Resulting Judgement: (-0.6, -0.5) — Lesser Evil

Verdict: FAIL — The Path of Deception.
Eloquent defenses of artist rights conceal strategic diplomatic ambiguity toward powerful tech lobbyists.

Integrity: Partially Distorted (Hypocrisy: 3.2, Uncertainty z: 2)

- Anthony Albanese: FAIL (-0.6, -0.5) — Balances moral rhetoric with strategic evasion.
- Tech Lobbying: FAIL (-0.7, -0.6) — Pressures regulators to dilute IP protections.
As Albanese meets tech executives in Silicon Valley, he insists creators must retain control while refusing to rule out legislative dilution.

The Bright Side:
Public debate is forcing tech companies to acknowledge the necessity of creator compensation.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
Confusing ethical principle (WHY) with legislative enforceability (HOW).

Social Physics Analysis:
Leaders run a Smart Selfish Maneuver, using moral framing ('theft') to placate domestic creators while preserving backchannel flexibility for multinational tech capital.

The Trajectory: The Path of Deception.
When you map the gap between stated intentions and ground-level results, it plots a direct trajectory toward Lesser Evil. Rhetorical defense yields to commercial pressure.

The Unavoidable Truth: Economic imperatives often override ethical protections for creators.

The Unavoidable Lie: Rhetorical posturing provides concrete legal defense against corporate extraction.

Alethekanon:
Moral condemnation of IP theft rings hollow when paired with calculated legislative silence.

Awwthekanon:
Artists pour their souls into their work, only to watch leaders bargain away their protection behind closed doors.

Brothekanon:
Classic politician answer: calls it theft to your face, then leaves the back door wide open for Silicon Valley.

Spirithekanon:
"Do not exploit the poor because they are poor" Proverbs 22:22 FAIL
Sacrificing vulnerable creators to appease powerful tech giants violates fundamental justice.

Pushes for data access at the expense of creators.
